sources.document: Publication 501 (2025), Dependents, Standard Deduction, and Filing Information

quotes.text: 12a Someone can claim: You as a dependent; Your spouse as a dependent. d You: Were born before January 2, 1961; Are blind. Spouse: Was born before January 2, 1961; Is blind.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Line 12d
quotes.text: If you or your spouse (if you are married and filing a joint return) were born before January 2, 1961, or were blind at the end of 2025, check the appropriate box(es) on line 12d. Don't check any boxes for your spouse if your filing status is head of household.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Line 12d (continued)
quotes.text: If your filing status is married filing separately and your spouse was born before January 2, 1961, or was blind at the end of 2025, you can check the appropriate box(es) on line 12d if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Line 12d, Death of spouse in 2025
quotes.text: Death of spouse in 2025. If your spouse was born before January 2, 1961, but died in 2025 before reaching age 65, don't check the box that says "Spouse was born before January 2, 1961." A person is considered to reach age 65 on the day before the person's 65th birthday. Example. Your spouse was born on February 14, 1960, and died on February 13, 2025. Your spouse is considered age 65 at the time of death. Check the appropriate box for your spouse. However, if your spouse died on February 12, 2025, your spouse isn't considered age 65. Don't check the box.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Line 12d, Death of taxpayer in 2025
quotes.text: Death of taxpayer in 2025. If you are preparing a return for someone who died in 2025, see Pub. 501 before completing the standard deduction information.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Line 12d, Blindness
quotes.text: If you weren't totally blind as of December 31, 2025, you must get a statement certified by your eye doctor (ophthalmologist or optometrist) that: You can't see better than 20/200 in your better eye with glasses or contact lenses, or Your field of vision is 20 degrees or less. If your eye condition isn't likely to improve beyond the conditions listed above, you can get a statement certified by your eye doctor (ophthalmologist or optometrist) to this effect instead. You must keep the statement for your records.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Line 12e, Standard Deduction, Exceptions 1 and 4
quotes.text: Exception 1—Dependent. Line 12a. If you checked a box on line 12a, use the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents to figure your standard deduction. ... Exception 4—Born before January 2, 1961, or blind. Line 12d. If you checked any box on line 12d, figure your standard deduction by using the Standard Deduction Chart for People Who Were Born Before January 2, 1961, or Were Blind if you are filing Form 1040 or by using the chart on the last page of Form 1040-SR.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents—Line 12e
quotes.text: Use this worksheet only if someone can claim you, or your spouse if filing jointly, as a dependent. 1. Check if: You were born before January 2, 1961. You are blind. Spouse was born before January 2, 1961. Spouse is blind. Total number of boxes checked. 2. Is your earned income more than $900? Yes. Add $450 to your earned income. Enter the total. No. Enter $1,350. 3. Enter the amount shown below for your filing status. Single or married filing separately—$15,750. Married filing jointly—$31,500. Head of household—$23,625. 4. a. Enter the smaller of line 2 or line 3. If born after January 1, 1961, and not blind, stop here and enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 12e. Otherwise, go to line 4b. b. If born before January 2, 1961, or blind, multiply the number on line 1 by $1,600 ($2,000 if single or head of household). c. Add lines 4a and 4b. Enter the total here and on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 12e.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Standard Deduction Chart for People Who Were Born Before January 2, 1961, or Were Blind
quotes.text: Don't use this chart if someone can claim you, or your spouse if filing jointly, as a dependent. Instead, use the worksheet above. [Boxes: You were born before January 2, 1961; You are blind; Spouse was born before January 2, 1961; Spouse is blind.] Single: 1 $17,750, 2 19,750. Married filing jointly: 1 $33,100, 2 34,700, 3 36,300, 4 37,900. Qualifying surviving spouse: 1 $33,100, 2 34,700. Married filing separately*: 1 $17,350, 2 18,950, 3 20,550, 4 22,150. Head of household: 1 $25,625, 2 27,625. * You can check the boxes for spouse if your filing status is married filing separately and your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return.

quotes.source: 2025 Instructions for Form 1040: Instructions for Form 1040, Schedule 1-A, Part V, Enhanced Deduction for Seniors
quotes.text: Fill out Schedule 1-A, Part V, only if: You (and/or your spouse if filing a joint return) were born before January 2, 1961. You have a valid social security number (SSN). If you are married filing jointly, the spouse who is claiming the enhanced deduction for seniors must have a valid SSN. Death of a taxpayer in 2025. If a taxpayer was born before January 2, 1961, but died in 2025 before reaching age 65, then the taxpayer doesn't qualify for the enhanced deduction for seniors. A person is considered to reach age 65 on the day before the person's 65th birthday. ... The maximum amount of the enhanced deduction for seniors is $6,000 per person. ... Married filing jointly—$150,000. Single, Head of household, or Qualifying surviving spouse—$75,000.

quotes.source: Publication 501 (2025), Dependents, Standard Deduction, and Filing Information: Publication 501 (2025), Higher Standard Deduction for Age (65 or Older), Death of taxpayer
quotes.text: Death of taxpayer. If you are preparing a return for someone who died in 2025, consider the taxpayer to be 65 or older at the end of 2025 only if the taxpayer was 65 or older at the time of death. Even if the taxpayer was born before January 2, 1961, the taxpayer isn't considered 65 or older at the end of 2025 unless the taxpayer was 65 or older at the time of death. A person is considered to reach age 65 on the day before the person's 65th birthday.

quotes.source: Publication 501 (2025), Dependents, Standard Deduction, and Filing Information: Publication 501 (2025), Higher Standard Deduction for Blindness
quotes.text: If you are blind on the last day of the year and you don't itemize deductions, you are entitled to a higher standard deduction.

quotes.source: Publication 501 (2025), Dependents, Standard Deduction, and Filing Information: Publication 501 (2025), Spouse 65 or Older or Blind, and Death of spouse
quotes.text: You can take the higher standard deduction if your spouse is age 65 or older or blind and: 1. You file a joint return, or 2. You file a separate return and your spouse had no gross income and can't be claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer. Death of spouse. If your spouse died in 2025 before reaching age 65, you can't take a higher standard deduction because of your spouse. Even if your spouse was born before January 2, 1961, your spouse isn't considered 65 or older at the end of 2025 unless your spouse was 65 or older at the time of death.

reading: Age: a box is checked for a person born before January 2, 1961. A person reaches 65 on the day before the 65th birthday, so January 1, 1961 counts and January 2, 1961 does not. A taxpayer or spouse who died in 2025 counts only if 65 at death (born February 14, 1960: death on February 13, 2025 counts; February 12 does not). The same test governs the senior deduction.
Blindness: totally blind on December 31, 2025, or the eye doctor's certified 20/200 or 20-degree statement. The instructions quoted do not say how blindness is judged for a person who died in 2025.

Spouse boxes: on a joint return; on a separate return only if the spouse had no income, isn't filing and can't be claimed as a dependent (the chart footnote and line 12d); never on head of household (line 12d). The chart's qualifying surviving spouse rows stop at 2 boxes, so only the taxpayer's boxes count on that status.

Amounts: chart single 17,750 / 19,750; joint 33,100 to 37,900; qualifying surviving spouse 33,100 / 34,700; separate 17,350 to 22,150; head of household 25,625 / 27,625. The dependents worksheet adds $2,000 per box (single, head of household) or $1,600 to the smaller of earned income plus $450 and the base. Senior deduction $6,000 per qualifying person, joint only for a married couple.
